contents.html: IPsec is the best-known protocol for protecting client-to-network and network-to-network traffic. IPsec is normally thought of as a protocol for virtual private networks (VPNs). A VPN creates a private data network while using public networks (typically the Internet) while providing both encryption and integrity protection to all data in the protected network. Most corporate firewall products include IPsec capabilities, making it much easier for a organization to connect their networks with IPsec at the same time as using firewalls to filter traffic. Note, IPsec can also be used to segment networks with cryptographic protection between each sub-network. Section 4 of NIST SP 800-77, Guide to IPsec VPNs, describes in detail how to use IPsec for secure network designs.
contents.html_ja: IPsec は、クライアントからネットワークへのトラフィックと、ネットワーク間のトラフィックを保護するための、最もよく知られたプロトコルです。IPsec は通常、仮想プライベートネットワーク（VPN）のためのプロトコルと考えられています。VPN は、パブリックネットワーク（通常はインターネット）を使いながらプライベートなデータネットワークを作り、保護されたネットワーク内のすべてのデータに暗号化と完全性保護の両方を提供します。ほとんどの企業向けファイアウォール製品には IPsec の機能が含まれているため、組織がファイアウォールでトラフィックをフィルタリングしながら、IPsec でネットワークを接続することがはるかに容易になります。なお、IPsec は、各サブネットワーク間に暗号による保護を設けてネットワークを分割するためにも使えます。NIST SP 800-77, Guide to IPsec VPNs の 4 節は、安全なネットワーク設計に IPsec を使う方法を詳しく説明しています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の画像と照合し一致。斜体を原本どおりに

contents.html: TLS/SSL can also be used to create VPNs, which are typically referred to as SSL VPNs. NIST SP 800-113, Guide to SSL VPNs, covers the technologies used in typical SSL VPNs. Section 2.2 of that document describes the common use cases for SSL VPNs, which are mostly for roaming access users, not fixed networks such as are typical in UOCAVA environments. In fact, SSL VPNs can be used in some of the same environments where IPsec VPNs are used, but they offer no greater security than IPsec VPNs. Choosing which type of VPN to deploy usually depends on the operational ease of use. If there are many remote access users with unmanaged PCs, SSL VPNs are often appropriate. If the network consists mostly or solely of gateway devices, then IPsec VPNs are usually more appropriate.
contents.html_ja: TLS/SSL も VPN の作成に使うことができ、これは通常 SSL VPN と呼ばれます。NIST SP 800-113, Guide to SSL VPNs は、典型的な SSL VPN で使われる技術を扱っています。同文書の 2.2 節は、SSL VPN の一般的なユースケースを説明していますが、これらは主に、UOCAVA 環境で典型的なような固定ネットワークではなく、ローミングするアクセス利用者向けです。実際、SSL VPN は、IPsec VPN が使われる環境の一部でも使えますが、IPsec VPN より高いセキュリティを提供するものではありません。どちらの種類の VPN を導入するかは、通常、運用上の使いやすさによって決まります。管理されていない PC を使う遠隔アクセス利用者が多数いる場合は、SSL VPN が適切であることが多くあります。ネットワークが主にゲートウェイ装置からなる、またはゲートウェイ装置のみからなる場合は、通常、IPsec VPN のほうが適切です。

contents.html: S/MIME is the most widely-used standard for digitally signing and/or encrypting email. Many email products come with S/MIME built in, and others have free S/MIME extensions that can be added easily. An email message that is signed with S/MIME before being sent can be checked by the recipient to be sure that no one has tampered with the message. A message that is encrypted with S/MIME prevents someone watching the network traffic from reading the body of the email message (although note the headers of the message are sent unencrypted). OpenPGP is a standard similar to S/MIME, and it is also widely used in email systems.
contents.html_ja: S/MIME は、電子メールにデジタル署名や暗号化、あるいはその両方を行うための、最も広く使われている標準です。多くの電子メール製品には S/MIME が組み込まれており、その他の製品にも、容易に追加できる無料の S/MIME 拡張があります。送信前に S/MIME で署名された電子メールメッセージは、受信者が、誰もメッセージを改ざんしていないことを確認できます。S/MIME で暗号化されたメッセージは、ネットワークトラフィックを監視している者が電子メールメッセージの本文を読むことを防ぎます（ただし、メッセージのヘッダーは暗号化されずに送られることに留意してください）。OpenPGP は S/MIME に類似した標準であり、これも電子メールシステムで広く使われています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の画像と照合し一致

contents.html: In order to use S/MIME effectively, both the sender and the receiver must share a mutually-trusted certificate authority (CA). There are many commercial CAs, although only some of them issue certificates for S/MIME. There are also many non-commercial CAs that might used by UOCAVA voters, including the US Government and US Department of Defense CAs. OpenPGP software usually uses a very different trust model than S/MIME, and does not normally have certificate authorities; this makes it harder to use in UOCAVA systems unless the voting jurisdiction already has a trust relationship with numerous other OpenPGP users.
contents.html_ja: S/MIME を効果的に使うには、送信者と受信者の両方が、相互に信頼する認証局（CA）を共有しなければなりません。商用の CA は数多くありますが、S/MIME 用の証明書を発行するのはその一部だけです。米国政府や米国国防総省の CA など、UOCAVA 有権者が使う可能性のある非商用の CA も数多くあります。OpenPGP ソフトウェアは通常、S/MIME とは大きく異なる信頼モデルを使っており、通常は認証局を持ちません。そのため、投票の管轄区が他の多数の OpenPGP 利用者とすでに信頼関係を築いている場合を除き、UOCAVA システムで使うのは困難です。

contents.html: As described in Section 2 of NIST SP 800-49, Federal S/MIME V3 Client Profile, different mail software supports different features of S/MIME, and network administrators need to be careful all systems can read and generate the S/MIME messages that are required for any voter information sent through secured email.
contents.html_ja: NIST SP 800-49, Federal S/MIME V3 Client Profile の 2 節で説明されているとおり、メールソフトウェアによって S/MIME の対応する機能が異なるため、ネットワーク管理者は、保護された電子メールで送られるあらゆる有権者情報に必要な S/MIME メッセージを、すべてのシステムが読み取り、生成できるように注意する必要があります。

contents.html: 5.4 Authentication of Endpoints

contents.html: Network security relies on at least one party in every communication being fully identified. In many cases, it relies on all parties being identified to the satisfaction of the other parties. In voting systems, these parties are most often human users (such as potential voters, system administrators, and auditor) and computer systems (such as web servers, email servers, and network infrastructure). Some methods for identifying human users and computer systems are similar, others are very different.
contents.html_ja: ネットワークセキュリティは、すべての通信において、少なくとも一方の当事者が完全に識別されていることに依存します。多くの場合、他の当事者が納得する形で、すべての当事者が識別されていることに依存します。投票システムでは、これらの当事者は、人間の利用者（投票しようとする有権者、システム管理者、監査者など）とコンピュータシステム（Web サーバー、電子メールサーバー、ネットワークインフラストラクチャなど）であることが最も多くあります。人間の利用者とコンピュータシステムを識別する方法には、類似したものもあれば、大きく異なるものもあります。

contents.html: The identities of users and systems are verified using authentication mechanisms. In many voting applications, it is very important to identify the user or system you are interacting with in order to not disclose information to, or receive forged information from, the wrong entities.
contents.html_ja: 利用者とシステムの ID は、認証の仕組みを使って検証されます。多くの投票アプリケーションでは、誤った相手に情報を開示したり、偽造された情報を受け取ったりしないために、やり取りしている利用者やシステムを識別することが非常に重要です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の画像と照合し一致

contents.html: A system may need to authenticate a user before granting them access to sensitive information or network services. For example, a voting jurisdiction probably wants to authenticate a person before allowing them to update their ballot delivery information; some jurisdictions may even require authentication before delivering blank ballots. Another typical use is authenticating users before allowing administration of networking systems and equipment.
contents.html_ja: システムは、利用者に機微な情報やネットワークサービスへのアクセスを許可する前に、その利用者を認証する必要がある場合があります。たとえば、投票の管轄区は、ある人が投票用紙の配布先情報を更新することを許可する前に、おそらくその人を認証したいと考えます。白紙の投票用紙を配布する前でも認証を求める管轄区があるかもしれません。もう 1 つの典型的な用途は、ネットワークシステムや機器の管理を許可する前に、利用者を認証することです。

contents.html: A user may need to authenticate a system before the user is willing to divulge personal information that can be used to impersonate the user later. For example, a user would want to be sure they are talking to a trusted server before the user gives his or her password or data used for password recovery such as their mother's maiden name. System-to-system communication often also relies on both systems being able to authenticate the others’ identity.
contents.html_ja: 利用者は、後で自分になりすますために使われうる個人情報を明かす前に、システムを認証する必要がある場合があります。たとえば、利用者は、パスワードや、母親の旧姓などパスワードの回復に使うデータを渡す前に、信頼できるサーバーと通信していることを確かめたいと考えるでしょう。システム間の通信も、両方のシステムが相手の ID を認証できることに依存していることが多くあります。

contents.html: Section 3 covered identification and authentication of users for both local access to machines and access to network resources. As described there, low-impact systems frequently use passwords over an encrypted channel to authenticate users. Medium-impact systems often require multi-factor to authenticate users. For high-impact systems, cryptographic hardware devices such as smart cards can be used to authenticate users.
contents.html_ja: 3 節では、マシンへのローカルアクセスとネットワークリソースへのアクセスの両方について、利用者の識別と認証を扱いました。そこで述べたように、影響度が低いシステムでは、暗号化されたチャネル上でパスワードを使って利用者を認証することが多くあります。影響度が中程度のシステムでは、利用者の認証に多要素認証が求められることが多くあります。影響度が高いシステムでは、スマートカードなどの暗号ハードウェア装置を使って利用者を認証できます。

contents.html: Authenticating machines normally involves stronger forms of authentication mechanisms. Instead of passwords or multi-factor authentication, machine authentication is almost always done with cryptographic authentication mechanisms using strong keys stored on the system. A strong key is one that contains so much unpredictable material an attacker could not possibly guess the key even if he or she used phenomenally expensive systems for an extremely long time.
contents.html_ja: マシンの認証は、通常、より強力な形態の認証の仕組みを伴います。マシンの認証は、パスワードや多要素認証の代わりに、システムに保存された強力な鍵を使う、暗号による認証の仕組みで行われるのがほぼ常です。強力な鍵とは、予測不可能な素材を非常に多く含むため、攻撃者が極めて高価なシステムを極めて長い時間使ったとしても、鍵を推測することが到底できない鍵のことです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の画像と照合し一致

contents.html: Machine authentication comes in two broad categories: those that use asymmetric public keys (such as digital signatures and public key encryption) and those that use shared secrets. Both can be equally secure for authenticating machines, but they are used quite differently in practice.
contents.html_ja: マシンの認証は、大きく 2 つの種類に分かれます。非対称鍵を使うもの（デジタル署名や公開鍵暗号など）と、共有シークレットを使うものです。マシンの認証には、どちらも同等に安全でありえますが、実際の使われ方は大きく異なります。

contents.html: Authentication based on public keys requires the verifier either have a copy of the public key or, more often, trust a third party that assures the public key given by the claimant is in fact theirs. The latter is how essentially all web browsers using TLS allow users to authenticate the servers to which they connect.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵に基づく認証では、検証者が公開鍵のコピーを持っているか、より多くの場合、請求者が示した公開鍵が実際に請求者のものであることを保証する第三者を信頼する必要があります。後者は、TLS を使うほぼすべての Web ブラウザーが、利用者が接続先のサーバーを認証できるようにしている方法です。

contents.html: Authentication based on shared secrets requires the two parties to have already exchanged the key they will use for communication. This exchange takes place out-of-band, meaning it uses a different protocol than the one being protected.
contents.html_ja: 共有シークレットに基づく認証では、2 つの当事者が、通信に使う鍵を事前に交換している必要があります。この交換は帯域外で行われます。すなわち、保護の対象となるプロトコルとは別のプロトコルを使います。

contents.html: If an attacker can get a copy of a machine’s authentication key, that attacker can impersonate the machine. In most current deployments, keys are stored on hosts on normal storage media such as hard drives. This relies on the security of the system to be as strong for protecting the keys as it is for protecting other system-critical information and processes. For example, most keys can only be read and written by someone who has the highest authorization access on a computer. Some high-impact systems store their keys in hardware using hardware security modules (HSMs). HSMs have much better properties to protect the keys from being read by an attacker, but rely on operational changes that are too onerous for many organizations.
contents.html_ja: 攻撃者がマシンの認証鍵のコピーを入手できれば、その攻撃者はそのマシンになりすませます。現在のほとんどの導入では、鍵は、ハードドライブなどの通常の記憶媒体上のホストに保存されます。そのため、鍵の保護には、システムのセキュリティが、他のシステムにとって重要な情報やプロセスの保護と同じ強度であることが前提になります。たとえば、ほとんどの鍵は、コンピュータ上で最高の認可アクセスを持つ人だけが読み書きできます。影響度が高いシステムの中には、ハードウェアセキュリティモジュール（HSM）を使って、鍵をハードウェアに保存するものがあります。HSM は、鍵が攻撃者に読み取られるのを防ぐ点ではるかに優れた特性を持っていますが、多くの組織にとって負担が大きすぎる運用上の変更が前提になります。

contents.html: Network devices such as web servers, mail servers, and firewalls, are normally identified to other devices using the cryptographic methods described above. These methods most commonly use digital certificates for identification. In a small number of voting systems, most notably with secure email, people are identified with certificates. In short, a digital certificate is a signed assertion that the cryptographic key in the certificate is associated with a particular person or system. Users of certificates rely on trusted third parties (often called “certificate authorities” or “CAs”) to make those assertions.
contents.html_ja: Web サーバー、メールサーバー、ファイアウォールなどのネットワーク機器は、通常、上述の暗号による方法を使って、他の機器に対して識別されます。これらの方法では、識別にデジタル証明書が使われることが最も多くあります。少数の投票システム、とりわけ保護された電子メールでは、人が証明書で識別されます。要するに、デジタル証明書とは、証明書内の暗号鍵が特定の人またはシステムに関連付けられていることを署名付きで表明するものです。証明書の利用者は、それらの表明を行うために、信頼できる第三者（しばしば「認証局」または「CA」と呼ばれます）に依拠します。

contents.html: In order for identification using certificates to be trustworthy, the secrets that are associated with the keys in certificates must be kept private; otherwise, an attacker who knows the secret could impersonate the holder of the keys. This requirement puts a lot of pressure on individuals to do proper key management. The three parts of NIST SP 800-57, Recommendation for Key Management, describe the issues with maintaining the secrecy of keys and the use of certificates for identification. In specific, Section 2 of Part 3 of this series lists many best practices for using keys in certificates.
contents.html_ja: 証明書による識別が信頼に足るものであるためには、証明書内の鍵に対応するシークレットを秘密に保たなければなりません。そうでなければ、そのシークレットを知る攻撃者が鍵の保有者になりすませてしまいます。この要件は、個人に適切な鍵管理を行うよう大きな負担をかけます。NIST SP 800-57, Recommendation for Key Management の 3 つのパートは、鍵の機密を維持することと、識別のための証明書の使用に関する問題点を説明しています。特に、このシリーズの Part 3 の 2 節は、証明書内の鍵を使う際の多くのベストプラクティスを一覧にしています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本の画像と照合し一致。斜体を原本どおりに

contents.html: In order for systems such as web browsers to work with certificates, they must have a set of trust anchors that are trusted to associate cryptographic keys with devices and people. A trust anchor is the key for a certificate authority who issues certificates (or authorizes others to do so on its behalf). The set of trust anchors used by an application or operating system is called the trust anchor store. Trust anchor stores must be managed carefully because if an attacker can get its own key in the trust anchor store of an application, or if he can subvert the trust anchor that is already in an application’s trust anchor store, the attacker can impersonate systems with whom the application communicates.
contents.html_ja: Web ブラウザーなどのシステムが証明書を扱うためには、暗号鍵を機器や人に関連付けることを信頼されているトラストアンカーの集合を持っている必要があります。トラストアンカーとは、証明書を発行する（または、その代理として他者に発行する権限を与える）認証局の鍵です。アプリケーションやオペレーティングシステムが使うトラストアンカーの集合は、トラストアンカーストアと呼ばれます。攻撃者が自分の鍵をアプリケーションのトラストアンカーストアに入れることができれば、あるいは、アプリケーションのトラストアンカーストアにすでにあるトラストアンカーを破壊できれば、そのアプリケーションが通信するシステムになりすませるため、トラストアンカーストアは慎重に管理しなければなりません。

contents.html: There are many different ways a CA might create a certificate for a web server or email user (the process is called enrollment although that term is rarely used on CA web sites). Because of this, when asking a CA to create a certificate for you, you need to first find their enrollment instructions and be sure they work for the web server or email client for which you want a certificate. Most often, the process involves telling your software to create a certificate request, delivering that certificate request to the CA, receiving email from the CA to validate you are authorized to request a certificate, performing that validation, and then receiving the certificate itself.
contents.html_ja: CA が Web サーバーや電子メール利用者のために証明書を作成する方法は、さまざまです（このプロセスは登録と呼ばれますが、この用語が CA の Web サイトで使われることはまれです）。このため、CA に証明書の作成を依頼する際には、まずその CA の登録手順を探し、それが、証明書を必要とする Web サーバーや電子メールクライアントで機能することを確かめる必要があります。ほとんどの場合、このプロセスは、ソフトウェアに証明書要求を作成させ、その証明書要求を CA に届け、証明書を要求する権限があることを検証するための電子メールを CA から受け取り、その検証を行い、その後に証明書自体を受け取るという流れになります。

contents.html: If your intended users do not already trust the CA with whom you have enrolled, those users must add a trust anchor for that CA in their web browser, email client, or operating system. Again, the steps to do this vary widely between different types of software. Also, note some users will be very hesitant to add a trust anchor because most software (for good reason) gives dire warning about adding trust anchors. In most cases, jurisdictions will be able to obtain certificates from a trust anchor supported by default in common browsers. - 29 -
contents.html_ja: 想定する利用者が、登録した CA をまだ信頼していない場合、それらの利用者は、Web ブラウザー、電子メールクライアント、またはオペレーティングシステムに、その CA のトラストアンカーを追加しなければなりません。ここでも、その手順はソフトウェアの種類によって大きく異なります。また、ほとんどのソフトウェアは（もっともな理由から）トラストアンカーの追加について重大な警告を出すため、トラストアンカーを追加することを非常にためらう利用者もいることに留意してください。ほとんどの場合、管轄区は、一般的なブラウザーで既定でサポートされているトラストアンカーから証明書を入手できるでしょう。 - 29 -

contents.html: Networks that have many individual users often want to limit who has access to the network, or at least limit access to certain parts of the network. This type of fine-grained admission to a network requires network access control, sometimes abbreviated NAC. NIST SP 800-46rev1, Guide to Enterprise Telework and Remote Access Security, particularly section 3 of that document, describes network access control systems and how they can be placed in a network to grant the specific access to users that a network administrator would want.
contents.html_ja: 多くの個人利用者がいるネットワークでは、ネットワークにアクセスできる人を制限したい、あるいは少なくとも、ネットワークの特定の部分へのアクセスを制限したいと考えることがよくあります。このような、ネットワークへのきめ細かなアクセス許可には、ネットワークアクセス制御（NAC と略されることもあります）が必要です。NIST SP 800-46rev1, Guide to Enterprise Telework and Remote Access Security、特にその文書の 3 節は、ネットワークアクセス制御システムと、ネットワーク管理者が望むとおりの特定のアクセスを利用者に付与するために、それらをネットワーク内にどのように配置できるかを説明しています。

contents.html: Security systems such as firewalls, VPNs, and network access control do not always succeed in the goal of keeping unwanted traffic from a network. Because of this, some network administrators deploy intrusion detection systems (IDSs) and intrusion prevention systems (IDPs) in parallel with firewalls to look for many different types of unwanted traffic. As explained in NIST SP 800-94, Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS), these devices are useful in profiling the type of traffic coming onto a network and looking for common attacks. However, managing IDSs and particularly IDPs can be very labor-intensive because most networks have complicated and hard-to-predict traffic patterns, in that these devices need to produce a lot of logs in order to be useful.
contents.html_ja: ファイアウォール、VPN、ネットワークアクセス制御などのセキュリティシステムは、望ましくないトラフィックをネットワークから排除するという目標を、常に達成できるとは限りません。このため、ネットワーク管理者の中には、さまざまな種類の望ましくないトラフィックを探すために、ファイアウォールと並行して、侵入検知システム（IDS）と侵入防止システム（IDPs）を導入する人もいます。NIST SP 800-94, Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS) で説明されているとおり、これらの装置は、ネットワークに入ってくるトラフィックの種類をプロファイリングし、一般的な攻撃を探すのに役立ちます。しかし、ほとんどのネットワークには複雑で予測の難しいトラフィックパターンがあり、これらの装置が役に立つためには大量のログを生成する必要があるため、IDS、特に IDPs の管理は、非常に労力のかかるものになりえます。

contents.html: As described earlier in this section, network segmentation can make management of each segment easier. Firewalls and VPN devices can be used to segment networks at their edges. In a LAN, however, network segmentation can be achieved more easily with managed switches. Low-end, unmanaged switches create fast connections based on traffic patterns, but managed switches also allow configuration to restrict access to certain ports (and therefore the networks connected to the ports) based on policies. Many managed switches allow access to a particular port based on authentication protocols using passwords and certificates. Managed switches cost much less than firewalls or VPNs, and they require much less setup and operational overhead to run.
contents.html_ja: 本節の前半で説明したとおり、ネットワークの分割は、各セグメントの管理を容易にできます。ファイアウォールと VPN 装置は、ネットワークの端でネットワークを分割するために使えます。ただし LAN では、マネージドスイッチを使うことで、ネットワークの分割をより容易に実現できます。低価格帯のアンマネージドスイッチは、トラフィックのパターンに基づいて高速な接続を作りますが、マネージドスイッチは、ポリシーに基づいて特定のポート（したがって、そのポートに接続されたネットワーク）へのアクセスを制限する設定もできます。多くのマネージドスイッチは、パスワードや証明書を使う認証プロトコルに基づいて、特定のポートへのアクセスを許可します。マネージドスイッチはファイアウォールや VPN よりもはるかに安価であり、運用に必要な設定作業や運用上の負担もはるかに少なくて済みます。

contents.html: Maintaining the security of electronic voting systems takes more than just planning and one-time execution of preventative steps: security must be monitored and acted on throughout the life of the system. Sections 4 and 5 of this document give advice about how to plan for protecting hosts and networks in a voting system, and discuss some aspects of how to maintain security day-to-day. However, IT threats faced by election system usually evolve, so paying attention to security every day can be just as important as planning and proper initial setup.
contents.html_ja: 電子投票システムのセキュリティを維持するには、予防的な手順の計画と一度限りの実行だけでは足りません。セキュリティは、システムの存続期間を通じて監視し、それに基づいて行動しなければなりません。本書の 4 節と 5 節は、投票システムのホストとネットワークを保護するための計画方法について助言し、日々のセキュリティの維持方法のいくつかの側面を論じています。しかし、投票システムが直面する IT の脅威は通常、進化するため、日々セキュリティに注意を払うことは、計画や適切な初期設定と同様に重要でありうるのです。

contents.html: The core practice for ongoing security is auditing of IT systems. Observing the statuses of the various parts of a system allows an administrator to find where the system is vulnerable to threats or, if not found ahead of time, the part of the system that was vulnerable to a successful attack. By their very nature, voting systems are subject to audits and record keeping to detect voter fraud. This section covers system audits and record keeping specific to host and network security that can be quite different than the type of attacks seen on non-electronic voting.
contents.html_ja: 継続的なセキュリティの中核となるプラクティスは、IT システムの監査です。システムのさまざまな部分の状態を観察することで、管理者は、システムが脅威に対して脆弱な箇所を見つけることができ、事前に見つけられなかった場合は、攻撃が成功した後に、脆弱だったシステムの部分を見つけることができます。投票システムは、その性質上、有権者による不正を検知するための監査と記録の保持の対象となります。本節は、ホストとネットワークのセキュリティに特有のシステム監査と記録の保持を扱います。これらは、非電子的な投票で見られる攻撃の種類とは大きく異なる場合があります。

contents.html: Some voting audits may also require IT system audits as one part of the overall audit. These voting audits will probably specify what type of auditing is needed for hosts and networks, but a jurisdiction should strongly consider going beyond the minimum required by voting audits for their IT auditing practices. Collecting more information can help detect attempted attacks that might be missed by collecting only the minimum amount of information required.
contents.html_ja: 投票の監査の中には、全体の監査の一部として IT システムの監査も必要とするものもあります。これらの投票の監査では、おそらくホストとネットワークに必要な監査の種類が指定されますが、管轄区は、IT の監査プラクティスについて、投票の監査で求められる最低限を超えることを強く検討すべきです。より多くの情報を収集することは、求められる最低限の情報だけを収集していては見逃される可能性のある、攻撃の試みの検知に役立ちます。

contents.html: It is relatively rare to see an attack in progress and recognize it as an attack, so keeping records of all audits is necessary. Good record keeping is useful for finding when and where an attack happened, but also for finding patterns of unsuccessful attacks as part of ongoing assessments about how to improve the security of a system. The value of the latter should not be underestimated: auditing stored audits can be very valuable to preventing attacks that take research on the part of an attacker.
contents.html_ja: 進行中の攻撃を目にして、それを攻撃だと認識することは比較的まれであるため、すべての監査の記録を保持することが必要です。優れた記録の保持は、攻撃がいつ、どこで起きたかを突き止めるのに役立ちますが、システムのセキュリティを向上させる方法についての継続的な評価の一環として、失敗した攻撃のパターンを見つけるのにも役立ちます。後者の価値を過小評価すべきではありません。保存された監査記録を監査することは、攻撃者側に調査が必要となる攻撃を防ぐために、非常に価値がありえます。

contents.html: Monitoring events can happen either in an automatic, continuous fashion, or sporadically by people who look through event logs and so on. Continuous monitoring is far more reliable for capturing data that can be used to analyze or prevent attacks, but sporadic monitoring by humans is required to detect anomalous events missed by automated programs. It is impossible to say either how detailed continuous monitoring records should be or how often sporadic human monitoring should take place: such judgments depend on the nature of the voting system and the value of various attacks to the attackers. Section 3 of NIST Draft SP 800-137, Information Security Continuous Monitoring for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, describes the process needed for both automatic and sporadic monitoring of networked computer systems.
contents.html_ja: イベントの監視は、自動的かつ継続的に行われる場合と、イベントログなどを調べる人によって散発的に行われる場合があります。継続的な監視は、攻撃の分析や防止に使えるデータを取得する点ではるかに信頼できますが、自動プログラムが見逃した異常なイベントを検知するには、人による散発的な監視が必要です。継続的な監視記録をどの程度詳細にすべきか、人による散発的な監視をどの程度の頻度で行うべきかを一律に述べることはできません。そのような判断は、投票システムの性質と、攻撃者にとってのさまざまな攻撃の価値によって決まります。NIST Draft SP 800-137, Information Security Continuous Monitoring for Federal Information Systems and Organizations の 3 節は、ネットワーク接続されたコンピュータシステムの自動監視と散発的な監視の両方に必要なプロセスを説明しています。

contents.html: Network security audits themselves need to be secured because they contain information that can be used to attack a network. For example, a typical audit will tell an attacker what the system administrators did not see when being probed for vulnerabilities. As described in NIST Draft SP 800-137, auditing information is normally kept offline or on systems that have different access control mechanisms than the systems that are being monitored.
contents.html_ja: ネットワークのセキュリティ監査自体も、ネットワークへの攻撃に使われうる情報を含んでいるため、保護される必要があります。たとえば、典型的な監査は、脆弱性を探る調査を受けたときにシステム管理者が何を見ていなかったかを、攻撃者に伝えてしまいます。NIST Draft SP 800-137 で説明されているとおり、監査情報は通常、オフラインで、または監視対象のシステムとは異なるアクセス制御の仕組みを持つシステムで保持されます。

contents.html: The audit logs for electronic voting systems can have even more stringent requirements than those of normal networked systems if they may contain information about voters that can be used to surmise those voters’ votes. Although it is unlikely these hosts contain actual votes, there are types of information that represent voting patterns that may be considered sensitive. If a log does not contain any personally-identifying information about voters or votes cast, the security of the log should be as high as for the logs of normal in-person voting. However, if the logged data (even if it is summarized data) contains more than what is available for in-person voting, the logs should probably be as secure as the data itself.
contents.html_ja: 電子投票システムの監査ログが、有権者に関する、その有権者の投票内容を推測するのに使える情報を含みうる場合、通常のネットワーク接続されたシステムのものよりも、さらに厳格な要件を課されることがあります。これらのホストに実際の票が含まれている可能性は低いものの、機微と見なされうる投票パターンを表す種類の情報があります。ログに、有権者や投じられた票に関する個人を特定できる情報がまったく含まれていないのであれば、そのログのセキュリティは、通常の本人が投票する形式の投票のログと同程度に高くすべきです。しかし、記録されたデータが（要約されたデータであっても）本人が投票する形式の投票で得られるもの以上の情報を含んでいる場合、そのログは、おそらくデータ自体と同程度に安全にすべきです。

contents.html: It is important the jurisdictions designing custom Internet-connected voting systems use current best practices in security. This is also true for jurisdictions selecting such systems from vendors: it is not sufficient to believe that all vendors are using security best practices that apply to each jurisdiction. Security practices are implemented by jurisdiction staff and contractors, so having all of those people be able to determine which practices are best is the first step to their implementation.

contents.html: Different positions have different roles and responsibilities for security. contents.html_ja: 職位によって、セキュリティに関する役割と責任は異なります。たとえば、データベース管理者のセキュリティ目標は、管轄区が使う Web サーバーのオペレーティングシステムを保守する人のものとは異なります。したがって、すべての職位について、セキュリティに関する役割と責任を明確に定義し、文書化することが重要です。

Operational Guidance
Handwritten signatures – This is the same type of token used by jurisdictions to authenticate local voters. Because it is easy to photocopy
- 7 -signatures, it is common to require that signatures used for authentication must be original signatures, not copies (i.e., signatures used for authentication purposes must be “wet signatures”).

Cryptographic Software – These are cryptographic keys that are stored on disk or some other unprotected media that typically must be unlocked before use (e.g., using a password). For example, the cryptographic keys might be stored in an encrypted format, using passwords to decrypt them.
- 8 -Authentication is accomplished by having the claimant interact with the verifier using a cryptographic protocol.
The tradeoffs for authenticating people who manage voting systems are quite different than those for authenticating voters. Many of the types of device-based

- 12 -tokens that are difficult in practice to distribute to voters, particularly remote voters, have much better security properties than passwords. Any small difficulty associated with distributing and administering these better mechanisms may be outweighed by their better security. That is, even if it is not terribly convenient for a system administrator to need to use a device-based authentication mechanism, doing so protects a system that itself protects the validity and secrecy of elections.

Voting system servers and management stations can be vulnerable to a wide variety of attacks from the Internet. Servers are normally at fixed, easily-determined locations, which makes a prolonged attack easier to mount. Management stations at fixed locations that are not protected by a firewall have a

- 14 -similar attack profile. In fact, management stations that are fully protected from the Internet can still be the target of attack if another computer on the protected network is compromised, such as by malware that was delivered in email or by web browsing.
Use strong authentication for every user who is allowed to administer the computer. Use of passwords that might be easily guessed or copied from
- 15 -other servers to which an attacker may have access is not strong enough for servers of high value.

Changes to the configuration of a voting server can have significant consequences on all aspects of the voting system. For example, a change to the networking software could cause some previously-acceptable communication to be rejected

- 16 -and previously-unacceptable communication to start being accepted. Another example is adding a piece of additional monitoring software: such a seemingly-benign change could slow the system significantly and/or possibly block the monitoring of existing software.

If new problems appear on the server, even after other changes have been applied, being able to look through the configuration change log can help pinpoint the changes that caused the problems; such monitoring is covered in section 3.4 of SP 800-128. There are many software packages that can be used to log configuration changes, but even keeping dated notes in a text file is better than

- 17 -nothing. Any configuration management should be done on a server other than the one that is being tracked, or at least the change database should be backed up to a different server so a change that is disastrous does not also take down the configuration management system itself.

The lifecycle of the software portion of a server or PC includes acquisition and modification, although rarely includes decommissioning. In this case, “acquisition” consists of two phases: purchasing and installation. Protecting a server during purchase is usually not an issue. However, Section 3.2 of SP 800-64rev2 describes how to perform risk assessment which is often overlooked in software purchasing. The methods used for installing purchased software, however, can have implications on security if the new software affects how previously-installed software performs. For example, adding software that

- 18 -purposely restricts the ability to use other software, such as anti-malware, can cause security problems if the blocked software is actually part of the security setup for the server. Thus, it is very important to monitor the logs of all server software after installing new software to be sure that the older software continues to perform as expected.

Constantly screen for cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities using firewalls and external screening services or web application scanners. Cross-site scripting is a mechanism for inserting scripts controlled by the attacker onto pages hosted on the web server. Their purpose is to gain access to private information that is used by the user’s browser, particularly

- 20 -site passwords and cookies. Most modern web browsers attempt to prevent cross-site scripting attacks by limiting the private information only to trusted web pages. However if an attacker can get their script onto a trusted page, they can masquerade as legitimate page content and access the private information.

The origin of messages sent over SMTP can be validated with three similar protocols: DKIM, SPF, and SenderID. Of the three, only DKIM is an Internet standard, and it is more widely deployed than the earlier SPF and SenderID

- 21 -protocols. Note that these protocols do not provide encryption or integrity protection; instead, they only allow the sending organization to assert that mail messages that claim to come from a particular domain name in fact do so.

There are many types of firewall devices, some of which are more appropriate for protecting networks of devices that are all controlled by a jurisdiction, but others of which are more appropriate for allowing outsiders (in this case, voters and those interested in registering) to have limited access to some of the computers

- 24 -in a protected network. Section 2 of SP 800-41rev1 describes each of the types of firewall devices that might be used. Jurisdictions that let voters have access to servers at the border or inside of its networks need to consider how to use web application firewalls and/or firewalls with network access control, and need to design their networks based on those choices.

To prevent such attacks, the public links in a network needs to be protected with cryptography. The two primary types of protection are encryption (the scrambling of data so an attacker cannot understand it) and integrity protection (preventing forged data from being accepted on the network). Encryption and integrity protection are usually provided at the same time. Even though it is technically feasible to have a network that provides integrity protection without
- 25 -encryption and vice versa, most businesses want both, so they use a single network protection system that provides both.

A system may need to authenticate a user before granting them access to sensitive information or network services. For example, a voting jurisdiction probably wants to authenticate a person before allowing them to update their

- 27 -ballot delivery information; some jurisdictions may even require authentication before delivering blank ballots. Another typical use is authenticating users before allowing administration of networking systems and equipment.

If an attacker can get a copy of a machine’s authentication key, that attacker can impersonate the machine. In most current deployments, keys are stored on hosts on normal storage media such as hard drives. This relies on the security of the system to be as strong for protecting the keys as it is for protecting other system-critical information and processes. For example, most keys can only be read and written by someone who has the highest authorization access on a computer. Some high-impact systems store their keys in hardware using hardware security modules (HSMs). HSMs have much better properties to protect
- 28 -the keys from being read by an attacker, but rely on operational changes that are too onerous for many organizations.

NIST’s FIPS 140 series of requirements and certifications is probably the best-known set of conformance and best-practice standards available. FIPS 140 is the anchor of a program at NIST called the Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP). US government agencies purchasing equipment that uses cryptography are required to verify the cryptography is certified to conform to FIPS 140, and
- 35 -other industries have also made FIPS 140 certifications into requirements as well. More information on CMVP and the FIPS 140 program can be found at <http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/STM/cmvp>.
In addition, a jurisdiction can create or purchase targeted ongoing training for people in specific security-sensitive roles, as described in Section 2.3 of SP800-

This can help assure that technical staff are proficient in the technologies with which they work. Training can also help election officials and their management understand the risk inherent in the decisions they make.

- 3 -This document refers to system designers, implementers, operators, auditors, and administrators as roles relative to the system used to support UOCAVA voting. Those terms may not directly correspond to job titles within the organization(s) assembling, procuring, deploying or maintaining these systems. For example, an individual who holds the title “System Administrator” in an organization’s IT department may be charged with designing and deploying a system that sends blank ballots via email.

- 19 -In order to assess the security of their backup system, jurisdictions need written backup procedures as part of the operational step of lifecycle management. These procedures list not only how the backup is made (such as what data is backed up and on what media), but also where and how the backups are stored and who has physical access to the backup media.

To reduce the likelihood of script injection attacks:

- 33 -When evaluating how well the technical qualifications that a person has are matched for the security skills needed for a particular role, many factors need to be taken into account. They may already have relevant, related experience in security-sensitive tasks such as operating and/or designing systems with security components; they may have certifications in security technologies; and they may have recent education or training without having the opportunity to use it.
- 34 -The latter category is often overlooked because it causes a large number of “false positive” reports, but it is a critical part of attack prevention.

If your intended users do not already trust the CA with whom you have enrolled, those users must add a trust anchor for that CA in their web browser, email client, or operating system. Again, the steps to do this vary widely between different types of software. Also, note some users will be very hesitant to add a trust anchor because most software (for good reason) gives dire warning about adding trust anchors. In most cases, jurisdictions will be able to obtain certificates from a trust anchor supported by default in common browsers. - 29 -Jurisdictions that want to be able to validate signed email from military personnel need to install the trust anchor for the US Department of Defense Root CA. This certificate can currently be found at <http://dodpki.c3pki.chamb.disa.mil/rootca.html>.

TLS is used to protect web-based traffic (that is, traffic run over the HTTP protocol).1 TLS is widely used for protecting point-to-point traffic, notably between a web client and a web server. TLS provides both encryption and integrity protection. Many protocols other than HTTP can be protected with TLS as well, but for voting jurisdictions, TLS is almost exclusively thought of in terms of web traffic.
1 TLS is the successor to SSL, and the two names are often used interchangeably.

Authentication typeSecurity ConsiderationsDeploying and Verifying
Handwritten signaturesCurrently universally used for in-person voting transactions, thus strong enough for remote transactions.If a ballot or information update form is delivered electronically, the claimant needs to have access to a printer. The claimant needs to be able to send the wet-signed paper to the verifier.
PasswordsUsers often use the same passwords at multiple sites and/or choose weak passwords, making impersonation attacks fairly easy. No hardware is required, making this the easiest electronic token available.Password can be chosen by the claimant or the verifier. Storing or transmitting unencrypted passwords makes attacks easier.
Identifying promptsGenerally not used for voting systems because the answers may be easy to guess or may be easy to determine from public systems.Prompts need to be chosen by the verifier. Storing unencrypted prompt responses makes attacks easier. Normally more than one type of prompt is used in a single system.
Printed sets of secretsCan be made secure against impersonation attacks by having the secrets be at least 40 bits long; these secrets are still easy to type.Verifier must get the printed material to the claimants, and claimants must have the material available when asserting their identity. Storage of secrets and prompts should be encrypted.
Out-of-band hardware accessThe verifier must assume that the hardware being accessed is still controlled by the claimant. For example, if the claimant has lost their cell phone, the new possessor can impersonate the claimant.A second communication system (such as a phone system) must be deployed and available to people who are doing the verification.

Single-factor One Time Password DeviceThese are usually small, hand-held cards and therefore can be lost or stolen. If these used as the only authentication factor, the new possessor could impersonate the claimant. Therefore, these should be used with another authentication factor, such as a memorized password.The claimant needs to be able to receive a short prompt and, within less than a minute, access the device and repeat back a short message from the device to the verifier.
Multi-factor One Time Password DeviceThese are usually small, hand-held cards and therefore can be lost or stolen. The new possessor has to be able to unlock the device (e.g., by guessing the PIN) in order to impersonate the claimant.The factor used to unlock the device must be set prior to deploying the device. This could be having users set or memorize a PIN, or having the device learn a biometric.
Cryptographic SoftwareThe security of the authentication mechanism depends on claimants keeping their private keys secret.The claimant needs to possess the private key, and the verifier needs to trust that the public key associated with the private key belongs to the claimant. Private keys are usually protected with passwords.
Cryptographic hardware devicesThese are usually small, hand-held cards and therefore can be lost or stolen. Many of these cards are protected with PINs or passwords; the new possessor has to be able to guess the password in order to impersonate the claimant. When implemented properly, this is a very strong authentication mechanism.The claimant needs to have a device that reads the cryptographic device (e.g., a smart card and card reader) connected to the computer they are using while authenticating.
